en: The Ritual Procedure for the Mahāpratisarā Vidyā.
Homage to the Blessed Noble Mahāpratisarā!
Having bowed with devotion to Pratisarā, who is praised by all the Buddhas,
I shall now write down that wheel for the prosperity of all sentient beings.

Being pure and composed, having offered the bali-oblation and other offerings, one should take a piece of birch bark or cloth measuring a closed fist in size, and first draw a single compartment measuring four finger-breadths.
In the center of that is the syllable *praṃ*, adorned with a half-moon and a bindu, and encircled by eight *hūṃ* syllables;
in the center of that is the mantra:
*oṃ maṇidhari vajriṇi mahāpratisare dhārakasya rakṣaṃ śāntipuṣṭiṃ kuru hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā*.
Then, on the outside, there are two folds of half a finger-breadth each.
There, in the first layer, the mantra is preceded by "Oṃ Maṇi" alone;
in the second, likewise, it is repeated twice;
then, on the outside, there is one layer three finger-breadths wide.
There, at the junctions of the two lines on the four petals of the lotus in the four directions, one should write the mantra in the sequence starting from the east.
Oṃ, O stainless one, O vast one, O most victorious one, O immortal one, grant protection to the holder! Hūṃ 2 Phaṭ 2 Svāhā!
In the south.
Oṃ amṛtavilokini, protector of the womb, attractor, perform protection, peace, and nourishment for the bearer! Hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā!
[In the west.]
Oṃ bhara bhara saṃbhara saṃbhara, O purifier of the faculties and powers, perform protection for the holder! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ ruru cale svāhā!
In the north.
Oṃ, O best of nectars, grant, grant, O most excellent and pure one, perform protection, peace, and nourishment for the holder; hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā!
In the center of the petals, within a *praṃ* syllable surrounded by eight *hūṃ* syllables, one should write the mantra beginning with "Maṇidharī" and so forth.
In the four intermediate directions, within the interior of half-vajras with four prongs, one should write the mantra in the sequence starting from the southeast corner.
Oṃ, O Vajrī of the bursting [fever], protect the wearer! Hūṃ 2 Phaṭ 2 Svāhā!
In the southwest.
Oṃ, bestower of nectar, protect the holder; hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā!
In the northwest: Oṃ vimale, protect the wearer! Hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā!
In the northeast: Oṃ jayavare, protect the holder; hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā.
At the eight junctions of the lotus petals and the half-vajras with three prongs, in the sequence of the directions beginning with the southeast:
Oṃ niśumbhavajriṇi, protect the wearer! Hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā!
Oṃ, O Śumbhavajrī, protect the wearer; hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā!
Thus, one should write the two mantras with one syllable intervening between them.
Then, on the outside, one should fashion four petals measuring half a finger-breadth each.
Then, on the first petal, one should write a single row of the syllable *hrīḥ*.
In the second: Oṃ aparājite mahādevi traṭ.
Oṃ kālakarṇi kṛt. Oṃ padmakuṇḍali paṃ. Oṃ puṣpadantini hūṃ.
Oṃ maṇyaṅkuśi hūṃ.
Oṃ vajraśṛṅkhale phuṃ / Oṃ śvete vaṃ / Oṃ mahāśvete phaṃ /
Oṃ mahākāli hrīḥ / Oṃ vajrarati kṛt / Oṃ vajrakāli hrīḥ /
Oṃ vajrapāśi pheḥ / Oṃ vajrapāśi bhṛt //
Oṃ vajrapāṇi mahābale dhīḥ / Oṃ vajramāle māṃ / Oṃ amṛtakuṇḍali svāhā /
Oṃ jvala 2 hūṃ phaṭ svaḥ / Oṃ ṭakki hūṃ jaḥ svāhā //
In the third: Oṃ cūḍe hrīḥ / Oṃ suvarṇakeśi kṛt.
Oṃ Piṅgale Laṃ.
Oṃ vidyunmālini jaḥ hūṃ / Oṃ śāntikari hūṃ / Oṃ puṣṭibalavardhani haḥ /
Oṃ śumbhakari hūṃ / Oṃ maṇidhari hūṃ //
Oṃ, wearer of the jewel crown and garland, hrīḥ!
Oṃ, Mahāpratisarā, praṃ!
Oṃ, dhuru dhuru, muru muru, huru huru, meru meru, hūṃ hūṃ!
Oṃ balavardhani hoḥ / Oṃ ruru cale hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā / Oṃ maṇidhari mahāpratisare, perform protection, peace, and nourishment for the wearer; hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā.
In the fourth: Oṃ tāre tām aḥ / Oṃ muḥ.
Oṃ āḥ, O Rākṣasī Ekajaṭā, jñāṃ!
Oṃ buddhe kṣitike he hūṃ!
Oṃ, O Skull-Bearer, hūṃ!
Oṃ Laṅkeśvarī Khaṃ!
Oṃ dhanye laṃ.
Oṃ keśini aṃ / Oṃ laṅkeśvari muḥ / Oṃ hārīti hāṃ hrīṃ //
Oṃ Pāñcike keṃ!
Oṃ, O Śaṅkhinī, saṃ kaṭ!
Oṃ, O Kūṭadantinī, kaṭ!
Oṃ, Śrī, O Goddess Śrī!
Oṃ, Sarasvatī, Baṃ! Oṃ, protect, protect the holder! [Mpvv]
From all fears, *dhīḥ*.
Oṃ, Goddess Śrī!
Oṃ, Padme Paṃ!
Oṃ, O wearer of the jewel, wielder of the vajra, hūṃ!
Oṃ locane lāṃ / Oṃ māmakī māṃ / Oṃ pāṇḍare pāṃ /
Oṃ vasudhāre vaṃ.
Oṃ kurukulle hrīḥ / Oṃ bhṛkuṭi bhṛṃ / Oṃ bhrūṃ hūṃ bhrūṃ āḥ // //
Then, on the outside, one should make a single fold measuring two finger-breadths.
There, one should draw forty-eight vajras with their tips pointing upward in a row.

At the junction of the two vajras, in the sequence of directions starting from the west, [the syllables are]: laṃ kṣuṃ kīṃ klūṃ īṃ bhrūṃ phaṃ maḥ khaṃ haḥ yāṃ jrīṃ āṃ hrīḥ rīṃ ḍrīṃ līṃ hīṃ suṃ kraṃ jaḥ dhāṃ proṃ hoḥ hūṃ āḥ phaṭ jaṃ smaṃ laṃ kaṃ baṃ ṛṃ plūṃ treṃ bhoṃ bhraṃ oṃ aṃ bhrāṃ kṣīṃ vīṃ heḥ jīṃ ruṃ rūṃ aṃ saṃ // 48 //
Then, one should construct a single enclosure outside that, measuring three finger-breadths in width.
There, one should draw forty-eight lotuses with eight petals each, fully blossomed, complete with filaments, and with stalks bound by ribbons.
Above that, one should draw forty-eight symbols.
A wheel, a sword, and a bow.
An arrow, a thunderbolt, or a mace.
The right-turning conch,
the Vajra-banner,
and the wish-fulfilling jewel.
A noose / An axe / A trident.
The goad; the parasol.
A lotus; a spear. // 16 //
Thus, having tripled [the mantra], one should write it.
All the syllables should be written with their heads facing outward.
The ritual procedure for the knowledge-mantra of the Noble Mahāpratisarā is completed.
